note: The regression corpus. Bill FILES are not kept here — this manifest is the shared definition, and `bun tools/corpus.mjs fetch` downloads them into corpus/files/, which is gitignored and never served. Add a bill by adding a row and re-running with --update.

bills.name: Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 (enrolled)
bills.why: Plain-text enrolled bill. Divisions and titles, a table of contents that lists both, and heavy Public Law / Statutes at Large citation.

bills.name: FRONTIER Act (H.R. 9925, sponsor PDF)
bills.why: PDF path with an indented line-number gutter. Freestanding: zero amendments is the correct parse, which is what makes it a good negative control.

bills.name: CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633, House-passed print)
bills.why: Typeset GPO PDF, densely amendatory. Doubled-single quotes, wrapped division headings, and both distributed 'Each of the following' instructions.

bills.name: CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633, Senate substitute text)
bills.why: The largest plain-text bill here. Mostly freestanding rewrite, reaches into title 11 (Bankruptcy), which no other bill does.

bills.name: CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633, House-passed text)
bills.why: The same bill as the House-passed PDF, in govinfo plain text. The pair is the only direct check that the two extraction paths agree on one document.

bills.name: Farm to Fly Act of 2025 (H.R. 1719, introduced)
bills.why: Small and entirely amendatory — its whole operative content is one instruction against 7 U.S.C. 8101. The redline case that matters: an anchored insertion ('inserting X after Y') rather than a strike-and-replace, reached by clicking the composed address rather than the amendment tag. That combination is what showed the redline was unreachable from a citation chip.

bills.name: Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (enrolled)
bills.why: Internal Revenue Code throughout — the one Act whose section numbers really are the Code's, so it exercises sectionsMatchCode. Also the corpus's short-title edge case: the enrolled text contains no 'may be cited as' at all, because the Senate struck the short title under the Byrd rule, so 'AMENDMENT OF 1986 CODE' is a faithful reading and not a parser fault. Do not re-investigate.

bills.name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (enrolled)
bills.why: The biggest bill in the corpus, ~3 MB. Titles 23 and 49, and enough structure to catch anything quadratic.

bills.name: Bipartisan Budget Act of 2018 (enrolled)
bills.why: Social Security Act and Medicare amendments in bulk — the offsetNote path, where Act section numbers do not match their 42 U.S.C. numbers.

bills.name: CARES Act (enrolled)
bills.why: Broad subject matter across many titles, and a bill that both creates freestanding programs and amends existing law in the same text.

bills.name: Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (enrolled)
bills.why: A Senate bill, so it exercises the S. designation rather than H.R. Amends title 18 in short, surgical instructions — the redline's best case.

bills.name: National Defense Authorization Act for FY2021 (enrolled)
bills.why: 4.7 MB, the largest text here. Title 10 throughout, with divisions, and enough repetition to expose anything quadratic.

bills.name: American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (enrolled)
bills.why: Social Security Act amendments in bulk, where Act section numbers diverge from their 42 U.S.C. numbers — the offsetNote path at scale.

bills.name: Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 (the Farm Bill, enrolled)
bills.why: About as amendatory as a bill gets: page after page of strike-and-insert against title 7, and the densest redesignation in the corpus.

bills.name: CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 (enrolled)
bills.why: Creates new programs and amends title 15 science authorities in the same text, with heavy internal cross-referencing between its own divisions.

bills.name: Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020 (enrolled)
bills.why: Carries the SECURE Act, so Internal Revenue Code amendments sit inside an appropriations vehicle — divisions, and IRC section numbers that are the Code's own.

bills.name: Great American Outdoors Act (enrolled)
bills.why: 15 KB. The smallest bill here and a useful floor: a short Act should produce a small, clean parse and nothing spurious.

bills.name: John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act (enrolled)
bills.why: Public lands: titles 16, 43 and 54, and a lot of Public Law and Statutes at Large citation rather than U.S. Code.

bills.name: Families First Coronavirus Response Act (enrolled)
bills.why: Small and fast-drafted, amending the FMLA, the Social Security Act and the Food and Nutrition Act at once. Emergency drafting is where odd phrasings turn up.

bills.name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (enrolled)
bills.why: 5.1 MB of omnibus. Many divisions, each a different Act, and the widest spread of citation kinds in the corpus.

bills.name: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (enrolled)
bills.why: The Social Security Act and Public Health Service Act at full scale — the two Acts whose section numbers diverge most sharply from their 42 U.S.C. numbers. The offsetNote path under maximum load.

bills.name: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (enrolled)
bills.why: A second, independent test of the 'Amendment of 1986 Code' declaration, in a bill that is nothing but Internal Revenue Code amendments from end to end.

bills.name: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (enrolled)
bills.why: Banking and securities: titles 12 and 15, and an Act that creates agencies while amending a dozen others. Heavy on 'such Act' anaphora.

bills.name: Every Student Succeeds Act (enrolled)
bills.why: Rewrites the Elementary and Secondary Education Act almost entirely — long redesignation chains and whole-part replacements against title 20.

bills.name: First Step Act of 2018 (enrolled)
bills.why: Criminal law: title 18 and title 34, short surgical amendments to sentencing provisions. A good redline case on a bill small enough to read.

bills.name: United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement Implementation Act (enrolled)
bills.why: Trade, title 19 — a corner of the Code nothing else here touches, and an implementing Act with a structure of its own.

bills.name: Water Resources Reform and Development Act of 2014 (enrolled)
bills.why: Title 33 and a great deal of uncodified Public Law amendment — the target family that was invisible until Public Laws became eligible targets.

bills.name: Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (enrolled)
bills.why: The oldest bill in the corpus by twenty years. Drafting conventions shift over time, and every parser here was written against modern text.

bills.name: USA PATRIOT Act (enrolled)
bills.why: 2001 drafting, ten titles, and amendments spread across titles 18, 31 and 50 — including a lot of 'such title' anaphora.

bills.name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019 (joint resolution, enrolled)
bills.why: A joint resolution rather than a bill, so the designation is H.J.Res. rather than H.R. — the one bill shape the meta parser has never been given.
